title: Balance and Proportion
summary: Balance distributes visual weight by task importance; symmetry is optional and decoration must not drive layout.

MUST.text: Allocate visual weight (size, color saturation, density, position) to critical information and actions first.
Use whitespace to isolate high-priority content; keep decorative elements subordinate in weight.

SHOULD.text: Prefer asymmetric layouts when tasks have unequal importance; align all blocks to the grid.
Keep primary content within a consistent measure (e.g., 60-75% of viewport) and secondary in the remainder.
Rebalance at breakpoints rather than forcing equal columns.

AVOID.text: Adding panels or cards solely to make columns look balanced.
Decorative imagery or color blocks heavier than task content.

DECIDE.decision: Give larger share to primary task
Remove or collapse, do not pad

EXAMPLE.good: "Operational queue takes 70% width; KPI tiles stack in 30% sidebar."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Two equal columns where one holds a single button."

FAILURE_MODES: Equal columns imply equal importance and dilute focus.
Decorative panels add noise without task value.
Responsive reflow can leave empty, padded regions.
Visual weight misaligned with task priority slows decisions.
